item.title: Harnessing regioselective aryl migration of pyridone-based aryl-λ3-iodonium salts to access iodine-substituted aryloxypyridines
item.dc:creator: Linmei Zhao
Mengling He
Wankai Ma
Zequan Xiang
Huaming Tao
Lijuan Song
Shaoyu Mai
item.description:
Authors: Linmei Zhao, Mengling He, Wankai Ma, Zequan Xiang, Huaming Tao, Lijuan Song, Shaoyu Mai
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract While 2- and 4-aryloxypyridines are ubiquitous in pharmaceutical molecules, efficient synthetic strategies—especially for synthesizing scaffolds with diverse multiple substituents on the pyridine core—remain limited. Here we show a hook-and-slide strategy for constructing these scaffolds, involving the in-situ generation of pyridonyl(aryl)iodonium salts from pyridones and Koser’s reagent (hook, C3 selectivity), followed by an iodine-to-oxygen aryl migration (slide, O selectivity). Such newly designed iodonium salts feature dual vicinal nucleophilic sites, and we demonstrate that using C2 − H imidazolium ionic liquids can exclusively transfer the aryl group to the strategic O site. This approach is transition-metal-free, scalable, and applicable to substrates with diverse electronic and steric properties or complex structures. Importantly, the resulting products retain −I and −NH 2 handles that are amenable to downstream derivatizations, enabling extensive exploration of previously inaccessible chemical space. The utility of this approach is further demonstrated through the concise synthesis of multiple pharmaceutical intermediates and a CRF 1 antagonist, CP-376395.

item.title: Disturbance increases soil microbiome functional redundancy but decreases capacity for insurance via winnowed environmental responsiveness
item.dc:creator: Samuel E. Barnett
Ashley Shade
item.description:
Authors: Samuel E. Barnett, Ashley Shade
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Coexisting populations performing similar functions (i.e., functional redundancy), can stabilize ecosystem outputs under disturbance. The insurance hypothesis proposes that diversity maintains community function under disturbance because functionally redundant taxa differ in their environmental responsiveness. However, how redundancy and insurance interact in microbial communities remains unclear. Here, we examine functional redundancy and insurance potential in soil microbial communities under long-term heat disturbance from an underground coal seam fire in Centralia, Pennsylvania, USA, using seven years of deep metagenome sequencing across heated and reference sites. Functional redundancy increases with disturbance intensity, driven by declines in taxonomic diversity and average genome size and by increased per-genome investment in biogeochemically relevant metabolisms (i.e., carbohydrate and nitrogen). However, a proposed proxy for environmental responsiveness, transcription factor evenness, is reduced in heated soils. These results indicate that prolonged, selective disturbance can enhance redundancy while simultaneously constraining insurance against future stress, shaping microbial community resilience under persistent disturbance.

item.title: Evolutionary plasticity of bacterial surface layer protein exoskeletons
item.dc:creator: Anna Barwinska-Sendra
Paula S. Salgado
Kacper M. Sendra
item.description:
Authors: Anna Barwinska-Sendra, Paula S. Salgado, Kacper M. Sendra
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11797
Abstract: Abstract All cellular life possesses environmental interfaces like cell membranes or cell walls, yet the compositional complexity of these major cell components limits structural and evolutionary studies. Prokaryotic surface layer (S-layer) exoskeletons, with their homopolymer paracrystalline architecture, offer a more tractable model of an environmental interface. However, extreme sequence diversity and heterogeneous multidomain organisation of S-layer proteins confound conventional evolutionary analyses. Here, by combining phylogenomics with structural modelling, we show that extensive sequence divergence, modular evolution and lateral gene transfer drive lineage-specific S-layer diversification across both monoderm ( Bacillaceae , Peptostreptococcaceae ) and diderm ( Caulobacteraceae , Deinococcaceae ) bacteria. Focusing on the Gram-positive order Peptostreptococcales , including environmental isolates and clinical pathogens, we uncover multiple S-layer architectures conferring divergent physiological properties. Molecular microbiology reveals that among close relatives utilising the same exoskeleton type, only pathogens display resistance to the antimicrobial immune effectors LL-37 and lysozyme. Furthermore, by experimentally determining two S-layer structures, we unravel how mechanisms including (intra)domain gains and losses generate hyper-diversity of homologous S-layers among clinical isolates of the pathogen Clostridioides difficile . Our findings establish the S-layer as a paradigm of molecular modularity and evolutionary plasticity. Specifically, evolution of a single structural protein enables rapid cell-surface reconfiguration and contributes to immune evasion in bacterial pathogens.

item.title: Protecting-group-lean platform for synthesizing diverse phenylethanoid glycosides uncovers antifibrotic leads
item.dc:creator: Banhao Kuang
Ruibo Lin
Gang Yang
Qian Zhang
Yu-Cheng Peng
Xinyang Jiang

item.description:
Authors: Banhao Kuang, Ruibo Lin, Gang Yang, Qian Zhang, Yu-Cheng Peng, Xinyang Jiang, Weiwen Wang, Kai Chen, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Phenylethanoid glycosides are structurally diverse natural products widely found in traditional medicinal plants and display a broad range of biological activities. However, systematic studies of their functions and structure–activity relationships have been limited by inefficient access to diverse analogs in useful quantities. Here we show a protecting-group-lean synthetic platform that provides a 29-member library of phenylethanoid glycosides with variations at four positions of the central glucose unit. The strategy combines regioselective glycosylation, β-selective glycosylation without neighboring-group assistance, selective caffeoylation, and a mild global deprotection that preserves labile caffeoyl esters. Two glycosylations and two additional transformations can be performed sequentially in one pot, substantially streamlining assembly. Biological evaluation in a TGF-β-induced fibroblast model reveals structure–activity relationships, provides insight into signaling pathways associated with antifibrotic activity, and identifies several compounds as promising leads for further antifibrotic studies.

item.title: Trypanosomes Maintain Propulsion in Confined Environments by Modulating Rotational Motility from Swimming to Network-Threading Propulsion
item.dc:creator: Narges Jamshidi Khameneh
Timothy Krüger
Patryk Nienaltowski
Marie Kater
Yves Emery
Dmitry A. Fedosov

item.description:
Authors: Narges Jamshidi Khameneh, Timothy Krüger, Patryk Nienaltowski, Marie Kater, Yves Emery, Dmitry A. Fedosov, Marco Polin, Markus Engstler
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11833
Abstract: Abstract The parasite Trypanosoma brucei lives in the body fluids of its hosts, including blood and interstitial fluids of various tissues. The mechanism of dissemination within these environments remains largely unresolved, although the trypanosome´s motility is known to play an essential role for its survival. The unicellular flagellate is a versatile microswimmer, like bacteria or sperm cells, albeit structurally more complex than these classical models. Here we study their motility in different viscous and elastic regimes. Using quantitative high speed video microscopy and digital holography microscopy, we detail the three-dimensional mechanical reaction of the flexible cell body with its uniquely attached flagellum to increasing confinement, leading to a network-threading type propulsion. This allows stable progressive motility despite a reduction in wave parameters up to tissue-like confinement. We thus show how trypanosomes can mechanically adjust in response to various microenvironments and, using flagellar beat reversal, manage the exploration of their complex environments.

item.title: Parental leave benefits and fathers’ postpartum mental health in Sweden
item.dc:creator: Amy Heshmati
Sol P. Juárez
item.description:
Authors: Amy Heshmati, Sol P. Juárez
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11639
Abstract: Abstract Mental health conditions in the postpartum period are common. Generous parental leave has been shown to protect against poorer postpartum mental health among mothers; however, evidence for fathers remains limited. We examine whether levels of paid parental leave benefits are associated with fathers’ mental health in the first year after childbirth in Sweden. Using national population registers, we include 210,285 first-time fathers whose children were born between 2007 and 2011. Fathers receiving basic benefits have higher odds of receiving any mental healthcare, being prescribed antidepressants or anxiolytics, and using specialist outpatient care than those receiving higher-level earnings-related benefits. The results are robust after adjusting for mental health history, income and employment status, though associations are attenuated. Fathers who do not take parental leave during the first year are more likely to receive any mental healthcare, specialist outpatient care or hospitalisation. Overall, fathers with access to more generous paid parental leave benefits experience better postpartum mental health. These findings suggest that well-compensated parental leave may benefit fathers’ mental health and promote gender equality in caregiving. However, further efforts are needed to determine whether parental leave systems mitigate or reproduce health inequalities given that parental leave benefit levels are contingent on labour market conditions.

item.title: Chiral SERS and photochemistry via collective hotspot asymmetry in metasurface-templated gold networks with disordered nanoscale porosity
item.dc:creator: Olga Guselnikova
Alina Gorbunova
Pavel Postnikov
Markus Valtiner
Jonathan P. Hill
Joel Henzie

item.description:
Authors: Olga Guselnikova, Alina Gorbunova, Pavel Postnikov, Markus Valtiner, Jonathan P. Hill, Joel Henzie, Daniel T. Payne, Martin Kartau, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Chiral molecules interact with light so weakly that discriminating enantiomers or driving enantioselective chemistry by using optical approaches requires intense circularly polarised lasers or complex resonant structures. Here we combine a geometrically disordered electrodeposited network with a lithographic chiral template resembling the shape of a shuriken. The resulting substrate generates superchiral fields that neither individual component produces. The mechanism underlying this anomalous response arises from two distinct effects: first, the shuriken structures generate substantial intrinsic optical chirality; second, the nanoporous network adds densely distributed plasmonic hotspots and an interference cross-term, which augments the local chirality even more prominently. This chiral plasmonic nanoporous network achieves not only ultrasensitive chiral detection by reaching the attomole range, but also introduces enantiospecific photochemical reactivity on a single substrate under continuous-wave linearly polarised light. Raman asymmetries approach the theoretical maximum ( ≈ 2), while enantiomeric excesses exceed 25%. Finally, a six-order-of-magnitude enhancement over conventional Raman optical activity was calculated.

item.title: Impacts of medications for obesity on global health and the environment
item.dc:creator: Roslyn C. Henry
Lindsay M. Jaacks
Kaia Waxenberg
Peter Alexander
item.description:
Authors: Roslyn C. Henry, Lindsay M. Jaacks, Kaia Waxenberg, Peter Alexander
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11638
Abstract: Abstract A new generation of medications for obesity could transform the global food system. While research has explored their health impacts, their implications for global food demand and land use remain unquantified. We apply a global food system model to project the impact of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1) uptake to 2050 among people with obesity under two scenarios: reduced calorie intake while maintaining dietary composition, and reduced calorie intake combined with shifts towards the EAT–Lancet diet. Compared with the Reference scenario, GLP-1-mediated calorie reduction alone results in up to 6.6 million avoided deaths globally in 2050 and 32 Mha more natural land area, reflecting reductions in cropland, pasture and managed forest. Combining GLP-1 use with EAT–Lancet dietary shifts increases these estimates to 7.7 million avoided deaths and 46 Mha more natural land. Lower food prices increase food consumption among untreated populations, including unhealthy foods, partially offsetting these gains.

item.title: Modulating FCC/HCP phase boundaries in inverse Co@BOx catalysts via crystal-phase-ratio variation for propane oxidative dehydrogenation
item.dc:creator: Shiqiang Xu
Yuhan Wang
Chunyao Fang
Xiaofeng Gao
Ziyu Song
Houhong Song

Haotian Zhang
item.description:
Authors: Shiqiang Xu, Yuhan Wang, Chunyao Fang, Xiaofeng Gao, Ziyu Song, Houhong Song, Zixuan Ma, Haotian Zhang, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract The oxidative dehydrogenation of propane offers a promising route to propylene, but developing low-temperature catalysts that simultaneously achieve high activity and selectivity remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report a Co@BO x inverse catalyst featuring engineered defects localized at face-centered cubic/hexagonal close-packed phase boundaries within the subsurface cobalt promoter. Using an oxidative atmosphere-induced exsolution strategy, we continuously tune the face-centered cubic/hexagonal close-packed phase ratio, maximizing the density of stacking faults at a 1:1 phase ratio. Catalytic activity exhibits a strong positive correlation with stacking fault density, with the optimal Co F/H-1.0 @BO x catalyst achieving 32% propane conversion and 83% olefin selectivity at 450 °C—5.1 times that of pristine cobalt boride. Density functional theory reveals that stacking faults modulate Co atomic spacing, weakening the excessively strong BO x -Co interfacial interaction. In situ spectroscopy demonstrates that maximized stacking faults strengthen O-H bonds in surface boron hydroxyl species and optimize radical initiation kinetics. This work establishes subsurface defect engineering as a potential strategy to enhance oxide overlayer reactivity in inverse catalytic systems.

item.title: Large electrocaloric effects in unannealed multilayer capacitors of partially ordered lead scandium tantalate
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Farenkov
Mengfan Guo
Jiaqi Zhang
Melony Dilshad
Nadia A. Stelmashenko
Xavier Moya

item.description:
Authors: Vladimir Farenkov, Mengfan Guo, Jiaqi Zhang, Melony Dilshad, Nadia A. Stelmashenko, Xavier Moya, Sakyo Hirose, Neil D. Mathur
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Multilayer capacitors of PbSc 0.5 Ta 0.5 O 3 with good B-site cation order ( S 111 ~ 0.9-0.96) are driven by supercritical fields of 15.8 V μm −1 in prototype coolers, such that large electrocaloric effects arise over a wide range of temperatures and peak to give thermocouple-measured temperature jumps of |∆ T j | ~ 4.0 K near room temperature. However, the high degree of B-site order requires an energetically expensive 42-day high-temperature anneal that would be economically expensive and environmentally damaging in mass production. Here we report that the performance reduction (4.0 K → 3.1 K) for unannealed multilayer capacitors of PbSc 0.5 Ta 0.5 O 3 with partial B-site order ( S 111 ~ 0.6) is surprisingly small because reduced latent heat is mitigated by high-field electrocaloric effects in the induced ferroelectric phase. Eliminating the anneal without unduly compromising performance should render unannealed multilayer capacitors of PbSc 0.5 Ta 0.5 O 3 attractive for applications.

item.title: Mitigating brittleness in ceramics via transformation- and twinning-induced plasticity
item.dc:creator: Yong Huang
Zhuo Chen
Kiana Rostamipour
Rainer Hahn
Verena Maier-Kiener
Jozef Keckes
Christian Mitterer
Nikola Koutná
item.description:
Authors: Yong Huang, Zhuo Chen, Kiana Rostamipour, Rainer Hahn, Verena Maier-Kiener, Jozef Keckes, Christian Mitterer, Nikola Koutná, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Ceramics usually exhibit inherent brittleness at room temperature due to their strong covalent/ionic bonding and few active slip systems. Consequently, ceramics exhibit a low damage-bearing capacity and typically sudden failure prior to yielding. Thus, achieving room-temperature plasticity while maintaining or enhancing the strength of ceramics remains critical and challenging. Here, we report a promising strategy to address this problem by concurrently activating twinning-induced plasticity and transformation-induced plasticity in a monolithic TaN ceramic film. Through precisely controlled physical vapor deposition, we stabilize the metastable δ-TaN phase with hierarchical nanotwinned architectures. Then, by combining micromechanical tests, atomic-resolution characterization, and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations, we demonstrate that the synergy of phase transformation and twinning brings exceptional damage tolerance and plasticity, achieving up to 60% compressive strain without catastrophic fracture alongside a hardness of ~43 GPa. Our work not only proves the feasibility of twinning and transformation-induced plasticity synergy in designing ultrahard and ductile materials, but also highlights the architecture optimization in nanotwinned ceramics.

item.title: Coherence toroidal vortices and statistic-veiled correlation topologies
item.dc:creator: Keyu Zhou
Yaning Zhou
Ao Zhou
Zhao Zhang
Jinzhan Zhong

Qiwen Zhan
item.description:
Authors: Keyu Zhou, Yaning Zhou, Ao Zhou, Zhao Zhang, Jinzhan Zhong, Houan Teng, Chunhao Liang, Qiwen Zhan, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 10612
Abstract: Abstract Toroidal vortices in fluid and gas dynamics underpin a broad spectrum of scientific and technological fields, from elementary particle physics to condensed matter systems, and have recently garnered significant attention in optics because of their inherent topological stability. Here we report the experimental observation of toroidal vortices in stochastic optical wavefields with partial coherence, termed coherence toroidal vortices, which eliminates deterministic topological signatures in conventional optical degrees of freedom while unveiling statistically hidden correlation topologies. These underlying topologies—including both fundamental and higher-order hopfionic textures—emerge in second-order field correlations and are accessible only through statistical measurements. We further examine the impact of chaotic channels on the stability of these statistically veiled correlation topologies, demonstrating that their topological invariants remain robust under realistic environmental perturbations. These findings are experimentally validated and offer novel insights into the potential of toroidal light vortices serving as controllable channels for directional energy and information transfer within complex media.

item.title: Estimating malaria burden in sub-Saharan Africa under intervention disruption using satellite-derived representations
item.dc:creator: Kaustubh Chakradeo
Alexandros Katsiferis
Neil Scheidwasser

Katherine E. Battle

item.description:
Authors: Kaustubh Chakradeo, Alexandros Katsiferis, Neil Scheidwasser, Iwona Hawryluk, Katherine E. Battle, Swapnil Mishra, David L. Smith, Seth Flaxman, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Malaria remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa. Stalled progress and funding constraints raise important questions about the dependence of current malaria burden on sustained intervention coverage. Here, we estimate malaria transmission potential under a low-intervention scenario where major malaria interventions are withdrawn while broader ecological and demographic conditions remain constant. We develop a contrastive representation-learning framework applied to 30-m Landsat 8 satellite imagery, integrating the resulting environmental representations within a Bayesian hierarchical model. This approach improves predictive accuracy over existing covariate-based malaria mapping methods. Using contemporary Global Burden of Disease 2024 population estimates, we estimate an annual malaria burden of 422 (275-582) million cases across sub-Saharan Africa, representing a 131% increase relative to current estimates. These findings quantify the structural vulnerability of malaria control gains across sub-Saharan Africa and reveal where intervention disruption could have the greatest impact.

item.title: A dual-anchoring mechanism for hemimethylated CG-guided histone ubiquitylation
item.dc:creator: Xinyi Chen
Zhongwen Cao
Daniel Li

item.description:
Authors: Xinyi Chen, Zhongwen Cao, Daniel Li, Jian Fang, Jiuwei Lu, Nelli Khudaverdyan, Stephanie Paspal, Yinsheng Wang, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Maintenance of plant CG DNA methylation requires VARIANT IN METHYLATION (VIM) proteins, a family of E3 ligases that couple hemimethylated CG (hemiCG) with histone ubiquitylation to regulate MET1-mediated DNA methylation. How the hemiCG readout guides VIM proteins for histone ubiquitylation remains unclear. Here we report structure-function characterization of VIM1-mediated histone ubiquitylation, revealing the N-terminal tails of H3 and H4 as the VIM1 substrates. The structures of VIM1 complexed with hemiCG-containing nucleosome and/or E2 UBC11 reveal that VIM1 is positioned over the nucleosome disk surface, with the RING2 and SRA domains anchored to the H2A-H2B acidic patch and linker hemiCG site, respectively, and the RING1 domain mediating UBC11 loading. The RING2-mediated anchoring helps position RING1 near the H3/H4 tails for substrate access, while the SRA-mediated anchoring antagonizes an autoinhibitory state. Together, such dual nucleosome anchoring by RING2-SRA mechanistically links the position-varying hemiCG mark to persistent, yet context-dependent H3/H4 ubiquitylation.

item.title: Superionicity and premelting of iron-rich (Fe,Mg)O at Earth’s core-mantle boundary
item.dc:creator: Wei Zhang
Tao Wang
Guilin Liu
Zhongfa Zhou
Duck Young Kim
Yu He
item.description:
Authors: Wei Zhang, Tao Wang, Guilin Liu, Zhongfa Zhou, Duck Young Kim, Yu He
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Core-mantle interactions are essential for understanding Earth’s interior dynamics and evolution. Experimental studies reveal that core-mantle reactions produce iron-rich (Fe,Mg)O (periclase‑wüstite solid solution). Here we show that Fe-rich (Fe,Mg)O exhibits pronounced superionic-onset and grain-boundary premelting behavior above ~0.9 T m ( T m : melting temperature). These effects are significant in (Fe x Mg 1-x )O (x > 0.8) under core-mantle boundary (CMB) conditions, causing elastic softening, enhanced elemental transport, and ultra-low viscosity. Enhanced diffusion may facilitate core-mantle reactions and the accumulation of Fe-rich material near the CMB, potentially contributing to a dense basal assemblage. Under mantle flow and/or thermal buoyancy, the low viscosity of connected Fe-rich (Fe,Mg)O could favor deformation and redistribution toward shallower depths. This process may contribute to the formation and evolution of some ultra-low velocity zones (ULVZs). The proposed scenario is consistent with the layered structures and inferred low viscosity of some ULVZs and suggests a potential role for Fe-rich (Fe,Mg)O in core-mantle material exchange and heat transfer.

Authors: Dandan Zheng, Changxu Liu, Qiang Yang, Yongqi Zhao, Shuangchun Wen, Hailu Luo, Shizhen Chen
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional materials exhibit pronounced layer-dependent properties, making accurate determination of atomic-layer thickness essential. Existing characterization techniques typically rely on spectroscopic signatures or scanning probes, which require complex instrumentation and often lack direct real-space interpretability. Here we introduce a spin-dependent optical differentiation approach that encodes thickness into directly observable edge features. By engineering the optical transfer function at planar interfaces, we access anisotropic and isotropic differentiation regimes governed by the spin Hall effect of light. In the anisotropic regime, the layer number is continuously encoded in the orientation of edge features. In the isotropic regime, a morphology-based transition, from disk to ring, provides a discrete and robust signature for layer identification. We experimentally demonstrate layer-resolved imaging in graphene, MoS 2 , and WSe 2 . Our results establish spin-dependent optical differentiation as a simple and versatile platform for translating atomic-scale variations into directly accessible optical features, enabling rapid and in situ characterization of two-dimensional materials.

Abstract: Abstract The practical deployment of high-energy-density lithium–oxygen batteries is fundamentally restricted by sluggish oxygen redox kinetics and the instability of discharge intermediates. Abstract: Abstract TROP it or drop it: Owing to fast magic-angle spinning at frequencies above 50 kHz, solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance has evolved as a versatile method to decipher protein structure, dynamics, and chemical properties. Abstract: Abstract Anodeless all-solid-state batteries with Ag-C interlayers offer high energy density and long cycle life, yet their operation in cold environments remains limited by poorly understood failure mechanisms. After 250 cycles at 5 °C, AAP-treated cells delivered approximately three times the discharge capacity of cells cycled with the fixed-temperature protocol. Abstract: Abstract Biomolecular thermodynamics and spectroscopy depend on relative conformer energies, local curvatures, and collective dipole fluctuations on the potential-energy surface. Conventional molecular mechanics force fields enable large-scale simulations, but their fixed functional forms can misrepresent infrared intensities, mode character, and environment-dependent vibrational response. Among models with explicit long-range electrostatics, SO3LR provides the best accuracy–cost balance of the models tested here. These results show that machine-learned force-field dynamics can recover collective, environment-dependent vibrational landscapes at near-DFT fidelity, enabling spectroscopically validated biomolecular simulations at force-field-like cost.

Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Realizing dipolar excitons that simultaneously exhibit strong optical activity and long-range repulsive interactions remains a central challenge in exciton-based nonlinear optics. This challenge stems from the intrinsic trade-off between achieving spatial charge separation, which is necessary for dipole formation, and maintaining sufficient wavefunction overlap to ensure efficient radiative recombination. Beyond addressing a key constraint in dipolar-exciton design, this work establishes frontier-state hybridization as a molecular design principle for constructing optically active, electrically polarized excitons in low-dimensional quantum materials.

Abstract: Abstract Reactive oxygen species (ROS) are essential redox messengers, yet their effects depend on concentration, localization, and duration. Abstract: Abstract Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes substantial infant morbidity and mortality, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Abstract: Abstract Cryo-focused ion beam (cryo-FIB) milling combined with cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) is a crucial technique for studying macromolecules in their native environment. Abstract: Abstract Deep-strong light-matter coupling is a non-perturbative regime of quantum electrodynamics in which the interaction strength exceeds the frequencies of uncoupled light and matter excitations. Whether a Dicke superradiant phase transition can occur in electronic systems with linear energy-momentum dispersion remains controversial because of the apparent absence of a diamagnetic A 2 term in their low-energy Hamiltonian. Our microscopic quantum theory and classical electromagnetic simulations are in agreement with measured spectra. We conclude that a diamagnetic A 2 term emerges despite the linear dispersion, preventing a Dicke superradiant phase transition.

Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is a major driver of the Earth’s climate, moving heat from the Southern Hemisphere to the Northern Hemisphere. Neither foraminiferal carbon isotope records nor modelling studies agree on the spatial extent of North Atlantic Deep Water (NADW), the northern deep limb of the AMOC, over the intensification of Northern Hemisphere Glaciation (iNHG, ~2.73 million years ago). In contrast, our reconstruction suggests very little glacial-interglacial variability in NADW extent during both the Late Pliocene and Early Pleistocene. These results suggest deep-water circulation was substantially different during a warm climate state, with implications for the role of NADW formation during major climate transitions and its future stability.

item.description:
Authors: Matthew N. McCarroll, Jarret A. P. Weinrich, Alyssa H. Marinas, Amanda Dombroski, Lain X. Pierce, Xilin Gu, Megan J. Larmore, Jinfeng Teng, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract General anesthetics are essential for invasive medical procedures; however, there remains a need for safer agents. Using a bespoke 96-well-plate format platform enabling high-throughput imaging of larval zebrafish behavior, we screen 12,000 compounds and identify an isoxazole chemotype that phenocopies the intravenous anesthetics etomidate and propofol. Its optimization via medicinal chemistry yields an anesthetic that we call nidradine. This anesthetic is efficacious in both zebrafish and mice and lacks the problematic adrenal suppression characteristic of etomidate. Mechanistic studies using electrophysiology and structural biology reveal that nidradine, like etomidate and propofol, is a positive allosteric modulator of the GABA A receptor. Remarkably, behavioral assays in mice demonstrate that nidradine differs from most general anesthetics in that it also produces analgesia at subsedative doses.

item.title: Leveraging sequence purification for accurate prediction of multiple conformational states with AlphaFold2
item.dc:creator: Enming Xing
Junjie Zhang
Shen Wang
Xiaolin Cheng
item.description:
Authors: Enming Xing, Junjie Zhang, Shen Wang, Xiaolin Cheng
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract AlphaFold2 (AF2) has transformed protein structure prediction by harnessing co-evolutionary constraints embedded in multiple sequence alignments (MSAs). MSAs not only encode static structural information, but also contain evolutionary signatures linked to protein dynamics and conformational heterogeneity, which are central to biological function. However, the subtle co-evolutionary signals that bias proteins toward distinct conformational states are often obscured by noise within MSA data and remain challenging to decipher. Here, we introduce AF-ClaSeq, a systematic framework that enriches and purifies state-specific evolutionary signals through iterative sequence classification and selection. By identifying sequence subsets that preferentially encode distinct conformational states, AF-ClaSeq enables robust predictions of alternative conformations across diverse protein systems. Our findings indicate that the accuracy of alternative-state prediction depends more on the purity of the evolutionary signal within an MSA than on sequence depth. Notably, purified sequences encoding specific structural states are distributed across phylogenetic clades and superfamilies, rather than being confined to individual lineages. By extending AF2 beyond single-state structure prediction, AF-ClaSeq provides a promising approach for exploring protein structural plasticity, establishing a foundation for future studies of the sequence determinants underlying conformational switching and allosteric regulation.

item.description:
Authors: Lauren M. Herr, Srijita Dhar, Martina Rossi, Ethan D. Schaffer, Kajal Biswas, Sandra S. Burkett, Ezgi Gül Keskin, Arindam Datta, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract The mechanistic basis for chromosomal instability characteristic of RECQ helicase disorders remains poorly understood due to their molecular-genetic complexity. To characterize the genetic interactions of RECQL1 ( also referred to as RECQL or RECQ1) , implicated in RECON syndrome, we performed an RNA interference screen and discovered a functional relationship with BLM , a gene that is mutated in Bloom syndrome. RECQL1/BLM co-deficient cells display pronounced replication stress, DNA damage accumulation, and chromosomal instability. Strikingly, RECQL1/BLM co-deficiency induces sister chromatid separation during metaphase suppressible by depletion of the cohesin unloader WAPL, suggesting that a threshold of replication stress in the genetically co-deficient cells disrupts cohesion. Primary embryonic fibroblasts from transgenic Blm -/- ;Recql -/- mice recapitulate the sister chromatid separation phenotype and heightened replication stress observed for human cells. Our findings highlight the joint roles of RECQL1 and BLM in the replication stress response and their concurrent importance for maintenance of chromosomal stability even in the absence of exogenously induced DNA damage. Furthermore, we elucidated a genetic interaction in which sister chromatid cohesion is synergistically elevated by the loss of two conserved RECQ helicases encoded by genes in which mutations are linked to hereditary diseases that are not associated with sister chromatid cohesion defects. The findings presented provide insights into the genetic crosstalk of two prominent RECQ helicases with established importance in clinical diseases of genomic instability.
